title: Kraków in Seven Days: Planty Ring, Kazimierz Nights, Nowa Huta Mornings
subRegion: Lesser Poland (Małopolska) — Kraków and the Wieliczka–Oświęcim corridor

bestPeriod.window: late April to mid-June, then the second half of September
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (Rynek Główny gridlock, Wieliczka queues, Kazimierz stag noise) and the first fortnight of December

hook: Most people give Kraków a weekend and see the Cloth Hall, a dragon and a queue. Seven days is the length at which the city stops performing. You get the hejnał at 07:00 with nobody watching, a whole grey morning in Nowa Huta's Plac Centralny, an unhurried afternoon in the Podgórze quarry, and enough evenings in Kazimierz to have a regular table. It is flat, compact, cheap by Western European standards, and it rewards patience more than energy.

itinerary.title: The Planty Ring and the First Hejnał
itinerary.morning: Arrive, drop bags, and walk the Planty clockwise from Barbakan to Wawel — 4 km, about an hour, and the fastest way to internalise the city's shape. It replaced the walls after 1820; the surviving fragment at Brama Floriańska tells you how thick they were.
itinerary.afternoon: Rynek Główny, then the Sukiennice gallery of 19th-century Polish painting upstairs in the Cloth Hall. Stand under St Mary's on the hour for the **hejnał** — played to four windows, cut off mid-phrase.
itinerary.evening: **Miód Malina**, ul. Grodzka 40 — pierogi and duck; touristed and still good. Nightcap at **Café Camelot**, ul. św. Tomasza 17.

itinerary.title: Wawel and the Renaissance Courtyard
itinerary.morning: Be at the Wawel ticket office when it opens; take the State Rooms first, then the Crown Treasury & Armoury. Timed slots mean a 09:30 entry and a 12:00 entry can be two hours apart.
itinerary.afternoon: Wawel Cathedral on its separate ticket: the Sigismund Chapel from the nave, the Royal Tombs below, then the timber climb to the Sigismund Bell. Descend through ul. Kanonicza, the city's best-preserved street.
itinerary.evening: **Starka**, ul. Józefa 14 in Kazimierz — house-aged rye vodkas and Galician cooking. Reserve; the back room fills by 19:30 [VERIFY: current hours].

itinerary.title: Under the Square, and Kazimierz After Dark
itinerary.morning: **Rynek Underground** — four metres below the square, the medieval market level with cloth stalls, cart ruts and a lead-smelting hearth. Ninety minutes is right.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross to Kazimierz. Szeroka's synagogue rectangle: the Old Synagogue (municipal museum), the Remuh with its 16th-century cemetery, then Izaak. Coffee and pistachio cake somewhere on ul. Józefa.
itinerary.evening: **Hamsa**, Szeroka 2, for hummus and mezze — the argument for Israeli food on this square is deliberate. Then a **zapiekanka** at the Okrąglak, the round former butchers' rotunda in the middle of Plac Nowy, roughly €4 (16–20 PLN) and open absurdly late [VERIFY: current prices and closing time].

itinerary.title: Oświęcim
itinerary.morning: Train from Kraków Główny to Oświęcim, then the shuttle or a 2 km walk to the Auschwitz I gate. Your booked English-language guided tour covers Auschwitz I and the bus transfer to Birkenau; allow 3.5 hours minimum.
itinerary.afternoon: Birkenau's scale is the point — the ramp, the wooden barracks, the distance from the gate to the ruins of Crematoria II and III. Do not schedule anything after it.
itinerary.evening: Back in Kraków, eat quietly and early. **Café Camelot** or a bowl of żurek near your flat. No nightlife tonight; nobody wants it.

itinerary.title: Podgórze, Zabłocie and the Ghetto Ground
itinerary.morning: Cross Kładka Bernatka to **Plac Bohaterów Getta** and its 70 empty bronze-and-steel chairs (Lewicki & Latak, 2005) — one per thousand deported. **Apteka pod Orłem**, the pharmacy on the square that stayed open through the ghetto, is a small, exact museum.
itinerary.afternoon: East into **Zabłocie**: Schindler's Factory on ul. Lipowa — a Kraków-under-occupation museum more than a Schindler shrine — then **MOCAK** next door.
itinerary.evening: **Bottiglieria 1881**, ul. Bocheńska 5 — tasting menu, Michelin-starred, book three to six weeks ahead; expect €90–€130 (380–550 PLN) per head with pairing [VERIFY: current menu price and hours].

itinerary.title: Nowa Huta and the Socialist City
itinerary.morning: Tram 4 or 22 from Teatr Bagatela to **Plac Centralny im. Ronalda Reagana**, 25–35 minutes. Walk the arcades, then out along **Aleja Róż** — a parade axis turned quiet rose-bed, with a hole where Lenin stood until 1989.
itinerary.afternoon: The Nowa Huta Museum branch and the Nowa Huta Underground shelters, then the concrete ark of Arka Pana church in Bieńczyce, built 1967–77 after a decade of refused permits [VERIFY: current opening hours for the shelter tours].
itinerary.evening: Back to Kazimierz for a slower night — wine on ul. Józefa, then Plac Nowy's bars, which are at their best on a Friday around 22:00.

itinerary.title: Wieliczka, Hala Targowa and the Mound
itinerary.morning: If it is a Sunday, start at **Hala Targowa** on ul. Grzegórzecka — the flea market runs early and thins out by 11:00; enamel signs, Cepelia textiles, and the grilled-sausage van under the viaduct [VERIFY: current market hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Train from Kraków Główny to Wieliczka Rynek-Kopalnia (24 min) for the **Tourist Route**: about 800 steps down, 3 km of the mine's 245 km walked, two hours underground, ending at the Chapel of St Kinga carved entirely from salt. Guided groups only; the mine now prices the Tourist Route seasonally from 93 PLN (~€22) per person, with a normal Polish-language ticket running roughly 100–130 PLN (~€23–€30) depending on the month [VERIFY: current foreign-language Tourist Route ticket price, which carries a premium over the Polish tour].
itinerary.evening: Tram 1 to Salwator, up ul. Kościuszki past the Norbertine convent to **Kopiec Kościuszki** for the last light over the Vistula bend, then a final supper back in Stare Miasto.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Copernicus
accommodationStrategy.description: on the quietest street inside the Planty, 200 m below Wawel, with a Renaissance-vaulted breakfast room and a rooftop looking straight at the cathedral. You walk everywhere and hear nothing at night.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–10 weeks ahead direct; rates jump for Corpus Christi and the Jewish Culture Festival.

accommodationStrategy.name: Karmel Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: one street off Szeroka but insulated from Plac Nowy's noise corridor, walking distance to Starka, Hamsa and the Kładka Bernatka footbridge to Podgórze. Best value for a seven-night stay.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; ask for a courtyard-facing room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Apartments on ul. Józefa or ul. Meiselsa
accommodationStrategy.description: over a week a kitchen and a washing machine change the economics. Buy at Stary Kleparz and cook two nights.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–8 weeks ahead; check for a lift and street-side double glazing.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming; 5G across the centre and Nowa Huta, free wifi on most MPK trams.
logistics.emergency: 112. The 24-hour *apteka* on ul. Karmelicka is the reliable central pharmacy.
logistics.weather: continental. April and October swing 8–20 °C in a day; winter smog (*smog krakowski*) is a genuine problem from November to February — another reason for the shoulder seasons.
logistics.bookingWindows: Auschwitz ~90 days; Bottiglieria 1881 three to six weeks; Schindler's Factory 5–10 days; Wieliczka and Wawel 2–7 days in shoulder season, longer in July.
logistics.money: złoty, not euro. Cards everywhere, including trams and market stalls. Refuse dynamic currency conversion at the terminal — always pay in PLN. Avoid Euronet ATMs on Floriańska; use a bank-branded machine. Roughly €1 ≈ 4.25–4.35 PLN [VERIFY: current exchange rate].
logistics.transportRules: validate nothing if you bought a mobile ticket — activate it *before* boarding. Inspectors work the Nowa Huta trams hard. The Wieliczka and Oświęcim trains are Koleje Małopolskie/Polregio; buy at the machine, not on board.
logistics.permits: photography without flash is fine in most museums but forbidden inside the Sigismund Chapel and in parts of Auschwitz; large bags (over 30x20x10 cm) are refused at the Auschwitz gate and there is no left-luggage inside.

proTips: Hear the hejnał at 07:00 rather than at noon. Same trumpeter, same broken note, an empty square, and you can actually see him lean out of the window.
Book the Auschwitz slot for a **13:00–14:00 start**, not 09:00. The morning coaches from Kraków clear Auschwitz I by early afternoon and Birkenau is nearly empty by 16:00.
Skip the Wieliczka organised coach tour. The Kraków Główny train plus a ticket bought at the mine costs about a third and you choose your own group.
Do Kazimierz on a Tuesday or Wednesday. Plac Nowy on a Saturday belongs to stag parties; midweek it belongs to Kraków.
Eat lunch at a *bar mleczny* — the milk bars on ul. Grodzka and in Nowa Huta serve naleśniki and barszcz for €3–€5 (12–20 PLN). It is the cheapest good food in the city.
For the Wyspiański windows at the Franciscan church, go between 15:00 and 16:30 on a clear afternoon; the west light is what the glass was designed for, and entry is free.
Ask for *"poproszę rachunek"* (the bill) and *"na wynos"* (takeaway). Tipping is 10% in restaurants, nothing in milk bars.

raw.Walkable neighbourhood blocks: **Stare Miasto within the Planty** — the 4 km green ring on the line of the demolished walls, enclosing Rynek Główny, ul. Floriańska, ul. Grodzka and ul. Kanonicza; nothing inside is more than 12 minutes' walk from the Cloth Hall. **Kazimierz** — the Szeroka rectangle (Remuh and Old Synagogues), ul. Józefa for galleries and small plates, Plac Nowy for the Okrąglak. **Podgórze** across the Powstańców Śląskich bridge — Plac Bohaterów Getta, ul. Lwowska ghetto-wall fragment, and the **Zabłocie** post-industrial strip along ul. Lipowa. **Nowa Huta**, 9 km east — Plac Centralny im. Ronalda Reagana and the fan of Aleja Róż, Aleja Solidarności and Aleja Jana Pawła II. **Salwator/Zwierzyniec**, at the western terminus of tram 1, for the Norbertine convent, ul. Kościuszki and the climb to Kopiec Kościuszki.
raw.Transit passes and prices: MPK single tickets are time-based, and the March 2026 tariff replaced the old 20-minute ticket with a 15-minute one — 15 minutes ~€0.95 (4 PLN), 30 minutes or one journey ~€1.40 (6 PLN), 60 minutes ~€1.85 (8 PLN), 90 minutes ~€2.10 (9 PLN); a 24-hour Zone I ticket is ~€4.65 (20 PLN), while the 48-hour ~€9.30 (40 PLN) and 72-hour ~€12.80 (55 PLN) tickets are sold only as all-zone versions (2026 KMK tariff). Buy from the on-board machine (card accepted) or the Jakdojade app. The **Kraków Card** bundles unlimited MPK travel with roughly 40 museums at about €30 for 24h, €45 for 48h and €52 for 72h, with a transport-free 72-hour museum pass at €30 (2026 tariff); note that Wawel and Wieliczka are outside it. Do the maths honestly: on a seven-day stay where your two biggest tickets (Wieliczka, Auschwitz) are *not* covered, singles plus individual admissions almost always win. Buy the Card only if you compress five paid museums into one 48-hour block.
raw.Cultural booking timelines: **Auschwitz-Birkenau** is the hard constraint. The guided-entry band is far wider than most guides admit: from April to September entry between 07:30 and 17:00 is only possible on a booked guided tour with an educator (to 16:00 in March and October, 15:00 in February, 14:00 in January and November, 13:00 in December), and the free individual entry cards are only for the hours outside that. Slots are released on visit.auschwitz.org daily at 12:00 noon, 90 days ahead, and English tours in the shoulder season are gone within days of release; the individual 3.5-hour guided tour is 150 PLN (~€35) in a foreign language, 140 PLN in Polish, and the six-hour study tour 190/180 PLN (2026 tariff). Book this before you book flights. **Schindler's Factory** (Fabryka Emalia Oskara Schindlera, ul. Lipowa 4) sells out most days by mid-morning — buy online 5–10 days ahead. **Wawel** uses timed entry per exhibition, with separate tickets for the State Rooms, Crown Treasury & Armoury and the Dragon's Den, and a limited free allocation on one weekday [VERIFY: current free-entry day and timed-slot rules]. **Wawel Cathedral** is ticketed separately at the office opposite the entrance, covering the Royal Tombs and the Sigismund Bell tower. **Rynek Underground** (Podziemia Rynku, entrance in the Cloth Hall's northern end) caps numbers and closes on the second Monday of each month; admission is ~€10.50 (45 PLN), reduced 35 PLN, and Tuesday is the free day, on a short 10:00–15:00 shift with no advance booking (2026 Muzeum Krakowa tariff). **Wieliczka** admits the Tourist Route in guided groups only.
raw.Architectural focal points: Gothic — **Kościół Mariacki** (14th c., asymmetric towers) and Veit Stoss's limewood altarpiece, 1477–89. Renaissance — the arcaded **Wawel courtyard** (Francesco the Florentine, from 1507) and Bartolomeo Berrecci's **Sigismund Chapel**, 1519–33, the purest Italian Renaissance interior north of the Alps. Młoda Polska / Secession — **Stanisław Wyspiański's** stained glass and wall painting at the Franciscan Basilica, ul. Franciszkańska 2, above all the west window *Bóg Ojciec — Stań się*. Socialist realism — **Nowa Huta** (from 1949), the Renaissance-quoting arcades of Plac Centralny and the axial Aleja Róż.
